features.caveats: Only absolute counts should be extracted; relative lymphocyte percentages are not acceptable substitutes.
features.description: The absolute number of lymphocytes per microliter of blood.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) from the pretreatment complete blood count (CBC) or laboratory report.
features.missing_value_rule: If the absolute lymphocyte count is not provided, represent as null.
features.name: absolute_lymphocyte_count
features.stability_summary: Absolute lymphocyte count is a standard hematologic parameter measured via CBC with differential, typically reported in thousands of cells per microliter.

features.caveats: Values may be labeled as 'ANC' or 'Neutrophils (absolute)'; extraction must ensure numeric consistency (e.g., 4.1 k/uL is equivalent to 4100 cells/µL).
features.description: The absolute number of neutrophils per microliter of blood.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the absolute neutrophil count (ANC) from the complete blood count (CBC) or laboratory results in the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the ANC is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: absolute_neutrophil_count
features.stability_summary: The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is a standard hematological measurement used clinically to assess the risk of infection and monitor chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression.

features.caveats: Dependence on the completeness of the Medication Administration Record (MAR) and clinician documentation of PRN medications.
features.description: Whether acetaminophen was administered to the patient during the pretreatment period.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if acetaminophen was administered by reviewing the medication administration record (MAR), medication orders, or clinical notes documenting the administration of the drug.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if documentation is absent or ambiguous regarding whether the medication was actually administered.
features.name: acetaminophen_administered
features.stability_summary: Administration of common analgesics like acetaminophen is typically well-documented in standardized medication records.

features.caveats: Absence of documentation does not definitively prove chemotherapy was not administered, but is the standard basis for a negative extraction in a clinical record.
features.description: Whether the patient received adjuvant chemotherapy following primary treatment.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if adjuvant chemotherapy was administered by searching for explicit mentions of 'adjuvant chemotherapy' or specific chemotherapy regimens (e.g., 'pemetrexed 4 cycles') documented as being given in the adjuvant setting.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the patient record contains no information regarding the administration of adjuvant chemotherapy.
features.name: adjuvant_chemotherapy_administered
features.stability_summary: Adjuvant chemotherapy administration is a standard, well-documented clinical event in oncology records.

features.caveats: The interpretation of 'suspicious' or 'likely' lesions as 'Present' depends on the clinical context provided in the radiology impression or oncology notes.
features.description: The presence of metastatic disease in the adrenal glands.
features.measurement_definition: Determine if the pretreatment clinical record (specifically radiology reports such as CT or PET/CT, or oncology progress notes) indicates the presence of metastatic lesions in the adrenal glands. This includes explicit mentions of 'adrenal metastasis', 'metastatic involvement' of the adrenal glands, or radiographic findings described as 'consistent with' or 'suspicious for' metastasis in the adrenal glands.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the adrenal glands are not mentioned or if the documentation is too ambiguous to determine presence or absence.
features.name: adrenal_metastasis_presence
features.stability_summary: Adrenal metastasis is commonly identified in lung cancer staging via CT or PET/CT imaging, appearing as abnormal masses or areas of increased FDG avidity.

features.caveats: Patients may have bilateral adrenal nodules; the ontology focuses on the maximum size for a patient-level scalar.
features.description: The maximum diameter of an adrenal nodule.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value of the largest adrenal nodule size reported in imaging (e.g., CT), typically measured in centimeters.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no adrenal nodule is documented or if the size is not specified.
features.name: adrenal_nodule_size
features.stability_summary: Adrenal nodule size is consistently reported as a linear measurement in centimeters using contrast-enhanced CT imaging.

features.caveats: Age may be reported as an integer or a range in some clinical texts; standardizing to a single scalar requires extracting the most specific numeric value.
features.description: The age of the patient at the time of the clinical encounter or index date.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the patient's age in years from the demographic section, pathology reports, or clinical narratives (e.g., '86-year-old', 'age 45').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if age is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: age
features.stability_summary: Age is a fundamental demographic variable consistently reported as a numeric value in years across the provided clinical evidence.

features.caveats: The provided evidence is sparse; the ontology assumes a binary representation of the presence of pathology in the airway based on the phrase 'likely central airway'.
features.description: Presence of pathological involvement of the airway.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient record or imaging reports indicate that the airway (specifically the central airway) is involved by a disease process.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the record does not mention airway involvement or is ambiguous.
features.name: airway_involvement
features.stability_summary: Based on radiological evidence suggesting central airway involvement.

features.caveats: Does not distinguish between the frequency of use or the specific formulation (e.g., inhaler vs. nebulizer).
features.description: Whether the patient uses albuterol.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient is using or has been prescribed albuterol (e.g., albuterol inhaler, albuterol nebulizer) within the pretreatment medical record, typically found in the medication list or respiratory history.
features.missing_value_rule: If albuterol use is not mentioned or is documented ambiguously, represent as null.
features.name: albuterol_use
features.stability_summary: Albuterol is a widely used beta-agonist bronchodilator commonly documented in medication lists and history of present illness for patients with obstructive airway diseases.

features.caveats: Quantitative extraction relies on the presence of 'drinks/week' or similar metrics; qualitative terms like 'occasional' without numbers may lead to imprecise values.
features.description: The average quantity of alcoholic beverages consumed by the patient per week.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the number of alcoholic drinks consumed per week. For ranges (e.g., '1-2 drinks/week'), calculate the mean. For reports of 'no alcohol use' or 'denies alcohol', extract as 0. If described as 'occasional' without a specific number, extract the numeric value if provided in the same context (e.g., 'occasional wine, <= 2 drinks/week' = 2).
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if alcohol use is not mentioned, not documented, or is too ambiguous to assign a numeric value.
features.name: alcohol_use
features.stability_summary: Alcohol consumption is consistently recorded in the social history of the provided evidence, appearing either as a specific numeric weekly count or as total abstinence.

features.caveats: Reference ranges for alkaline phosphatase can vary by laboratory and patient age/sex.
features.description: The patient's serum alkaline phosphatase level.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) reported in laboratory results, typically as part of a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP).
features.missing_value_rule: If the alkaline phosphatase level is not documented or is ambiguous, represent as null.
features.name: alkaline_phosphatase_level
features.stability_summary: Alkaline phosphatase is a standard clinical laboratory measurement of enzyme activity in the blood, typically reported in units per liter (U/L).

features.caveats: The provided evidence is minimal; categories are defined based on standard clinical practice for documenting functional mobility.
features.description: The patient's functional ability to walk or move from one place to another.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the patient's reported or observed ability to ambulate from the pretreatment record, specifying if they are independent, require assistance (including assistive devices), or are unable to walk.
features.missing_value_rule: If ambulation status is not documented or is ambiguous, it is represented as null.
features.name: ambulation_status
features.stability_summary: Ambulation status is a standard clinical metric for assessing functional independence and disease progression.

features.caveats: The supporting evidence is a brief list of medication classes, providing minimal context on dosage or specific drug names.
features.description: Whether the patient is using anticoagulant medication.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient is documented as using anticoagulant medications in the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if anticoagulant use is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: anticoagulant_use
features.stability_summary: Evidence indicates the presence of anticoagulants within a list of current medications.

features.caveats: Documentation may list specific antihypertensive drug names (e.g., Lisinopril, Amlodipine) rather than the general term 'antihypertensive'.
features.description: Patient use of antihypertensive medications.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is documented as taking antihypertensive medication from the pretreatment medical records, medication lists, or clinical history.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if antihypertensive medication use is not mentioned or is ambiguous.
features.name: antihypertensive_use
features.stability_summary: Medication history is a standard component of clinical documentation and generally stable across record types.

features.caveats: Anxiety may be described with qualifiers such as 'mild' or 'occasional' and may be situational (e.g., related to treatment).
features.description: Presence of anxiety symptoms or a diagnosis of anxiety during the pretreatment period.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient record mentions the presence of anxiety in the psychiatric or psychosocial sections, or within the history of present illness. Any mention of anxiety, regardless of severity (e.g., 'mild anxiety', 'occasional anxiety'), is extracted as 'Present'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Absent' if there is no mention of anxiety in the provided clinical documentation.
features.name: anxiety_present
features.stability_summary: Clinical evidence shows patients may report mild or occasional anxiety, often linked to their medical condition or treatment.

features.caveats: Dose may be mentioned without a specific numeric value in some records (e.g., 'on atorvastatin').
features.description: The daily dose of atorvastatin prescribed to the patient prior to treatment.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of the atorvastatin dose from the medication lists or clinical notes.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if atorvastatin is not mentioned or if the medication is listed without a specific dose.
features.name: atorvastatin_dose
features.stability_summary: The clinical evidence consistently represents atorvastatin dosing as a numeric value in milligrams (mg).

features.caveats: The ontology classifies EGFR status as a binary state and does not distinguish between specific mutation types (e.g., Exon 19 deletion vs. L858R).
features.description: The mutation status of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) biomarker.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the reported EGFR mutation status from pretreatment records. Map 'wild type' or 'negative' to 'Wild type' and 'mutant', 'positive', or specific named EGFR mutations to 'Mutant'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent absent or ambiguous documentation as null.
features.name: biomarker_egfr_status
features.stability_summary: EGFR status is a somatic genomic marker; while generally stable, different biopsy sites or modalities (tissue vs. liquid biopsy) may yield conflicting results, which are resolved by prioritizing the detection of a mutation.

features.caveats: The feature name suggests a biomarker status (typically genomic), but the supporting evidence explicitly mentions 'ml/min', which is the standard unit for Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR).
features.description: Patient's glomerular filtration rate measurement.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value of the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) reported in ml/min from the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent missing or ambiguous GFR documentation as null.
features.name: biomarker_fgfr_status
features.stability_summary: The provided unit 'ml/min' identifies this feature as a measurement of kidney function (GFR) rather than a protein/gene mutation status.

features.caveats: The ontology is derived from a small set of evidence; other common biopsy methods not mentioned in the text are not included.
features.description: The technique or procedure used to obtain the tissue biopsy specimen.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the specific method used to obtain the biopsy specimen (e.g., bronchoscopic, needle biopsy) from the procedure or pathology documentation.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no biopsy method is documented.
features.name: biopsy_method
features.stability_summary: The feature is supported by explicit mentions of 'specimen bronchoscopic' and 'needle biopsy' in the clinical evidence.

features.caveats: Denosumab is a bone-modifying agent but not a bisphosphonate; it should be excluded from this specific feature extraction unless the text explicitly classifies it as such.
features.description: Whether the patient is currently receiving or has a documented history of bisphosphonate therapy.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is receiving or has received bisphosphonate therapy. This is identified by explicit mentions of 'bisphosphonate' or specific bisphosphonate medications (e.g., zoledronic acid, pamidronate, alendronate) in the medication list or clinical narrative.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if bisphosphonate therapy is not mentioned or is explicitly denied in the record.
features.name: bisphosphonate_therapy_status
features.stability_summary: The patient has a documented history of using zoledronic acid for symptomatic hypercalcemia and ongoing skeletal-related event prophylaxis, confirming the use of bisphosphonate therapy.

features.caveats: Extracting only the systolic component from a systolic/diastolic pair may omit relevant diastolic information.
features.description: The patient's blood pressure, specifically the systolic value.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the blood pressure measurement from the pretreatment record. When blood pressure is recorded as a systolic/diastolic pair (e.g., 128/78 mmHg), extract the systolic (first) value. If only a single numeric value is provided for blood pressure, extract that value.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if blood pressure is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: blood_pressure
features.stability_summary: Blood pressure is a standard clinical vital sign routinely measured and reported in mmHg.

features.caveats: BUN levels can be influenced by factors other than renal function, including high-protein diets, dehydration, and gastrointestinal bleeding.
features.description: A measurement of the amount of nitrogen in the blood that comes from the urea produced by the liver, used primarily to assess renal function.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of blood urea nitrogen (BUN) from the comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) or specific renal function laboratory tests.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the value is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: blood_urea_nitrogen
features.stability_summary: BUN is a standard clinical laboratory measurement reported numerically, typically with the unit mg/dL.

features.caveats: BMI may be explicitly reported or derivable from height and weight if available.
features.description: The patient's body mass index (BMI), a measure of body fat based on height and weight.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value for BMI in kg/m² from the pretreatment record, typically located in the vital signs or physical examination sections.
features.missing_value_rule: If BMI is not documented and cannot be calculated from height and weight, the value is null.
features.name: bmi
features.stability_summary: BMI is a standard clinical metric for quantifying body mass relative to height.

features.caveats: Weight may be reported in pounds (lbs) in some records, requiring conversion to kilograms for standardization.
features.description: The patient's body weight recorded prior to the start of treatment.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of the patient's body weight in kilograms (kg). If the value is reported in pounds (lbs), convert it to kilograms.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if body weight is not documented or cannot be reliably extracted.
features.name: body_weight
features.stability_summary: Body weight is a standard clinical anthropometric measurement used for dosage calculations and health assessment.

features.caveats: The provided evidence only explicitly mentions 'lytic lesion'; other categories (blastic, mixed) are included to complete the clinical ontology for bone lesion morphology.
features.description: The morphological characteristic of bone lesions identified in the patient record.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the described type of bone lesion morphology (e.g., lytic, blastic, or mixed) from the musculoskeletal or oncology sections of the clinical record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no specific morphology is documented.
features.name: bone_lesion_characteristics
features.stability_summary: Evidence specifically identifies a 'lytic lesion' associated with the spine and vertebral body, treated with zoledronic acid.

features.caveats: The sensitivity of different imaging modalities (e.g., bone scan vs. PET/CT vs. MRI) varies; a negative result on one may not preclude the presence of metastases identified by another.
features.description: Presence of bone metastasis at the time of pretreatment.
features.measurement_definition: Determine if there is any documentation of bone or osseous metastasis in the pretreatment record, typically extracted from radiology reports (e.g., bone scan, PET/CT, CT, MRI) or oncology assessment notes.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if bone metastasis is not mentioned or the documentation is too ambiguous to determine presence or absence.
features.name: bone_metastasis_presence
features.stability_summary: Bone metastasis is a well-established clinical feature in advanced cancer staging, typically confirmed via radiographic evidence of lytic or sclerotic lesions in the skeletal system.

features.caveats: Patients may report pain in multiple skeletal locations; this scalar ontology captures a single primary or most recent location.
features.description: The anatomical location of the patient's reported or observed bone pain.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the anatomical region of the skeleton associated with reported bone pain, tenderness during physical examination, or documented symptomatic bone metastases (e.g., 'T8' or 'thoracic spine' maps to 'Thoracic spine'; 'L3', 'low back', or 'lumbar spine' maps to 'Lumbar spine'; 'femur' maps to 'Femur').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no bone pain location is documented or if bone pain is mentioned without a specified location.
features.name: bone_pain_location
features.stability_summary: Bone pain location is consistently documented in clinical notes through patient reports in the history of present illness or tenderness noted during the musculoskeletal physical examination, often correlating with imaging evidence of fractures or metastases.

features.caveats: Bone pain is frequently documented using varied terminology such as 'back pain' or 'bone discomfort' in the context of skeletal metastases; these are treated as equivalent to bone pain.
features.description: Presence of bone pain during the pretreatment period.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether bone pain is documented in the pretreatment records. This includes explicit mentions of 'bone pain', 'bone discomfort', or 'back pain' when it is associated with osseous metastases (e.g., 'thoracic bone pain', 'lower-back pain radiating to the left flank', or 'right femoral pain').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if bone pain is neither documented as present nor explicitly denied in the record.
features.name: bone_pain_status
features.stability_summary: Bone pain is a frequently reported symptom in patients with skeletal metastases in the provided text, appearing across various patient profiles with consistent descriptors related to spinal and pelvic discomfort.

features.caveats: The ontology assumes a binary classification of the BRAF status; specific variants (e.g., V600E) are grouped into the 'Mutated' category.
features.description: Presence or absence of a pathogenic mutation in the BRAF gene.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the BRAF mutation status from molecular profiling or next-generation sequencing (NGS) reports. 'Wild-type', 'no pathogenic variants', or 'no mutations identified' map to 'Wild-type'. The identification of any activating mutation (e.g., V600E) or a label of 'Mutated' maps to 'Mutated'.
features.missing_value_rule: If the BRAF status is not documented or the documentation is ambiguous, the value is represented as null.
features.name: braf_mutation_status
features.stability_summary: BRAF mutation status is a genetic marker that typically remains stable throughout the clinical course of a tumor.

features.caveats: Evidence is limited to a single mention of 'edema no' within a neurological/radiological context.
features.description: The presence or absence of brain edema.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the status of cerebral edema from radiology reports (e.g., MRI T2 FLAIR) or neurological clinical evaluations.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if brain edema is not documented or the status is ambiguous.
features.name: brain_edema_status
features.stability_summary: The evidence indicates the feature is tracked as a binary status, specifically noting the absence of edema in the provided snippet.

features.caveats: The count may be limited by the resolution of the imaging modality used (e.g., PET/CT may miss small lesions detectable on MRI).
features.description: Total number of discrete lesions identified within the brain parenchyma.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the total number of distinct, discrete intracranial lesions (such as enhancing nodules, masses, or FDG-avid foci) reported in the neuroimaging findings. If the report explicitly states 'no lesions' or 'no abnormal uptake', the value is 0.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no brain imaging is documented or if the report does not specify the number of lesions.
features.name: brain_lesion_count
features.stability_summary: The count of brain lesions is a standard quantitative radiological metric used to assess metastatic burden and monitor treatment response in oncology.

features.caveats: For lesions with multiple dimensions reported (e.g., 1.2 cm x 1.0 cm), the largest dimension is used. In cases of multiple brain lesions, only the diameter of the largest lesion is extracted to provide a single patient-level scalar.
features.description: The maximum diameter of the largest brain lesion.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the largest dimension in centimeters of the largest brain lesion identified on brain MRI. If only one dimension is provided, use that value. If multiple dimensions are provided for a single lesion, extract the maximum of those values.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no brain lesions are identified, if brain imaging was not performed, or if the size of the lesion is not specified.
features.name: brain_lesion_size
features.stability_summary: Lesion size is standardly reported in clinical radiology as the maximum diameter in centimeters.

features.caveats: Laterality (left/right) is not captured in this scalar ontology; only the anatomical lobe is extracted.
features.description: The anatomical location of brain metastases within the cerebral lobes.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the specific cerebral lobe(s) where brain metastases are identified in the pretreatment imaging or clinical reports (e.g., Occipital, Parietal, Frontal, Temporal).
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no brain metastases are documented or if the specific lobe location is not mentioned.
features.name: brain_metastases_location
features.stability_summary: The feature is supported by clinical text identifying metastases in the occipital and parietal lobes.

features.caveats: Imaging quality, such as motion-degraded MRI, may result in an 'unknown' or 'uncertain' status even when imaging was performed.
features.description: Presence of brain metastases
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether brain metastases (intracranial lesions) are present or absent based on radiographic evidence (e.g., brain MRI, CT) or clinical documentation in the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the record contains no information, explicitly states the status is unknown or uncertain, or if imaging was inconclusive due to technical limitations.
features.name: brain_metastases_presence
features.stability_summary: The presence of brain metastases is established via neuroimaging, typically contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain, which is the standard for staging in non-small cell lung cancer.

features.caveats: Does not distinguish between specific brain structures if multiple are mentioned; focuses specifically on abnormal enhancement.
features.description: Presence of abnormal contrast enhancement in brain structures.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient record reports 'abnormal enhancement' or 'contrast enhancement' within brain structures (e.g., brainstem, cerebellum, or ventricles).
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if there is no mention of abnormal enhancement or if the documentation is ambiguous.
features.name: brain_structure_enhancement
features.stability_summary: Based on radiologic reporting of contrast enhancement patterns in brain structures.

features.caveats: The evidence contains fatigue data from multiple instruments (PRO-CTCAE and EORTC QLQ-C30); this ontology specifically targets the PRO-CTCAE grade as it is the standard representation of severity.
features.description: The severity of cancer-related fatigue as measured by the PRO-CTCAE (Patient-Reported Outcomes Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events) scale.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric PRO-CTCAE grade for fatigue, typically represented as an integer from 0 (none) to 4 (very severe).
features.missing_value_rule: If no PRO-CTCAE fatigue grade is explicitly documented, the value should be represented as null.
features.name: cancer_related_fatigue_severity
features.stability_summary: The clinical text demonstrates the use of a 0-4 grading scale (PRO-CTCAE) to quantify fatigue severity, which is a standard oncology metric.

features.caveats: Requires post-contrast imaging for accurate detection; lack of contrast administration may result in an inability to determine enhancement status.
features.description: Presence of abnormal contrast enhancement in the cavernous sinuses.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether post-contrast imaging (e.g., gadolinium-enhanced T1-weighted MRI) indicates abnormal enhancement of the cavernous sinuses. Report 'Present' if abnormal enhancement is identified and 'Absent' if the report explicitly states 'no abnormal enhancement' or describes the cavernous sinuses as 'unremarkable'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the cavernous sinuses are not mentioned or if the imaging was performed without contrast.
features.name: cavernous_sinus_enhancement
features.stability_summary: Based on standard neuroradiological assessment of post-contrast MRI sequences to identify inflammatory or neoplastic processes in the cavernous sinus.

features.caveats: Signal intensity is a qualitative radiological assessment that varies by MRI sequence; findings are collapsed into a binary status.
features.description: Qualitative assessment of the MRI signal intensity of the cerebellar hemispheres.
features.measurement_definition: From the neuroimaging report (specifically the posterior fossa or brain parenchyma sections), extract whether the signal intensity of the cerebellar hemispheres is described as normal or abnormal.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the cerebellar hemisphere signal is not mentioned or is undocumented.
features.name: cerebellar_hemisphere_signal
features.stability_summary: Cerebellar signal intensity is a standard neuroradiological observation used to identify pathology such as ischemia, edema, or inflammation.

features.caveats: If multiple different chemotherapy regimens are listed with separate cycle counts, the extraction should target the total cumulative count unless specified otherwise.
features.description: The total number of chemotherapy cycles administered to the patient.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical count of chemotherapy cycles mentioned in the record (e.g., '4 cycles' or 'four cycles').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the number of cycles is not documented or cannot be determined from the text.
features.name: chemotherapy_cycle_count
features.stability_summary: The feature is supported by explicit mentions of chemotherapy cycle counts associated with adjuvant treatment.

features.caveats: The available evidence provides a limited set of chemotherapy regimens; actual clinical records may contain a broader variety of agents.
features.description: The specific chemotherapy agent or combination of agents administered to the patient.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the name of the chemotherapy drug or the specific combination of drugs (e.g., 'Cisplatin + Pemetrexed', 'Pemetrexed', 'Taxane-based') identified in the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent missing or ambiguous documentation as 'Unknown'.
features.name: chemotherapy_regimen
features.stability_summary: The supporting text explicitly mentions pemetrexed, cisplatin combined with pemetrexed, and taxane-based therapy.

features.caveats: None
features.description: Whether the patient has a documented history of cholecystectomy.
features.measurement_definition: Extract from the patient's past medical or surgical history whether they have undergone a cholecystectomy (surgical removal of the gallbladder).

features.name: cholecystectomy_history

features.caveats: The ontology does not distinguish between Stage 3a and 3b, treating both as Stage 3 unless otherwise specified in the record.
features.description: The documented stage of chronic kidney disease (CKD).
features.measurement_definition: Extract the explicitly stated stage of chronic kidney disease (CKD), typically reported as a number from 1 to 5 (e.g., 'CKD stage 3').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the CKD stage is not explicitly documented.
features.name: chronic_kidney_disease_stage
features.stability_summary: CKD staging is a globally recognized clinical standard based on glomerular filtration rate (GFR) levels.

features.caveats: The provided evidence is minimal; the set of categories is inferred based on the typical clinical use of the term 'intermediate' within phenotyping scales.

features.measurement_definition: Extract the documented clinical phenotype classification from the pretreatment record, specifically identifying categories such as intermediate, mild, or severe.

features.name: clinical_phenotype
features.stability_summary: The phenotype classification categorizes the patient's clinical presentation, with 'intermediate' representing a mid-range manifestation of the disease.

features.description: Presence of a documented history of community-acquired pneumonia.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient has a documented diagnosis, history, or hospitalization for community-acquired pneumonia from the medical record.
features.missing_value_rule: If there is no mention of community-acquired pneumonia in the record, represent as 'Absent'.
features.name: community_acquired_pneumonia_presence
features.stability_summary: The evidence explicitly documents a hospitalization for community-acquired pneumonia at age 93 and lists it within the past medical history.

features.caveats: The count is dependent on the comprehensiveness of the documented medical history and the specific criteria used to distinguish a comorbidity from the primary diagnosis.
features.description: The total number of distinct comorbid medical conditions documented in the patient's pretreatment record.
features.measurement_definition: Count the number of unique diagnosed medical conditions present in the patient record, excluding the primary diagnosis for which the patient is being treated.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 0 if no comorbidities are documented; represent as null if the record is missing or unable to be parsed.
features.name: comorbidities
features.stability_summary: Comorbidity count is a standard clinical measure used to assess baseline health status and risk stratification.

features.caveats: The ontology captures the binary presence of confusion regardless of frequency (e.g., 'intermittent') or severity.
features.description: Presence of confusion as a clinical symptom.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if confusion is documented as a symptom in the patient's clinical record, such as in the chief complaint or history of present illness.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'absent' if not mentioned or explicitly denied in the record.
features.name: confusion_present
features.stability_summary: Confusion is a standard clinical finding often reported in neurologic assessments and chief complaints.

features.caveats: Extraction is dependent on explicit documentation of a COPD diagnosis; patients with undiagnosed or unlabelled obstructive lung disease will be marked as absent or missing.
features.description: The presence of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) prior to the start of treatment.
features.measurement_definition: Identify whether the patient has a documented diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) within the past medical history, problem list, or clinical assessment sections of the pretreatment record.

features.name: copd_presence

features.description: Presence of edema surrounding the tumor as identified on radiographic imaging.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if the pretreatment imaging records explicitly state the presence or absence of peritumoral (surrounding) edema.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if edema is not mentioned or if the documentation is too ambiguous to determine presence or absence.
features.name: peritumoral_edema
features.stability_summary: The feature is based on radiographic evidence of surrounding edema, a standard clinical observation in tumor imaging.

features.caveats: Detection is dependent on the MRI sequences performed (e.g., FLAIR); the absence of a mention in a report may not definitively rule out the abnormality if the appropriate sequences were not acquired.
features.description: Presence of abnormal signal intensity in the white matter surrounding the cerebral ventricles on neuroimaging.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the presence or absence of 'periventricular signal abnormality' or 'periventricular white matter signal changes' from the radiology findings or impression.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the radiology report does not mention periventricular signal intensity or if the documentation is ambiguous.
features.name: periventricular_signal_abnormality
features.stability_summary: This is a standard binary radiological finding used to identify leukoencephalopathy, small vessel disease, or other white matter pathologies.

features.caveats: Pathway activation is typically inferred from the presence of activating mutations in the PIK3CA gene rather than a direct functional measurement of pathway activity.
features.description: Presence of PI3K pathway activation, typically identified through molecular profiling of the PIK3CA gene.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the status of PI3K pathway activation from molecular pathology or Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) reports. The feature is 'Activated' if the report identifies activating mutations in PIK3CA (e.g., H1047R, E545K) or explicitly states 'PI3K pathway activation'. The feature is 'Not Activated' if the report explicitly states that no activating PIK3CA mutations were detected or that the pathway is not activated.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the PI3K pathway status is not documented or the report is ambiguous.
features.name: pi3k_pathway_activation
features.stability_summary: PI3K pathway activation is a recognized molecular alteration in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), often associated with PIK3CA mutations, which can influence therapeutic response to EGFR inhibitors and guide enrollment in PI3K-targeted clinical trials.

features.caveats: Values are typically reported in thousands per microliter; notations such as 'k', '10^3/uL', and 'k/uL' are treated as numerically equivalent.
features.description: the number of platelets per microliter of blood, reported in thousands (k/uL)
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value for platelets (Plt) from the Complete Blood Count (CBC) in the pretreatment record. Report the value in thousands per microliter (k/uL); for example, if the value is 210,000/uL, extract 210.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the platelet count is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: platelet_count
features.stability_summary: Standard hematological measurement provided in Complete Blood Count (CBC) results.

features.caveats: Qualitative descriptions are used as quantitative volume measurements are rarely provided in the text.
features.description: The presence and qualitative volume of fluid accumulation in the pleural space.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the descriptive status of pleural effusion from the most recent imaging reports (e.g., CT, PET/CT, Chest X-ray) or clinical notes. Map 'no pleural effusion' or 'none' to 'Absent', and qualitative descriptors such as 'small', 'moderate', or 'large' to their respective categories.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if there is no mention of pleural effusion or if the documentation is too ambiguous to categorize.
features.name: pleural_effusion
features.stability_summary: Pleural effusion is consistently reported in thoracic radiology and clinical notes, typically described qualitatively by size or as absent.

features.caveats: The evidence specifically mentions community-acquired pneumonia and ICD-10 code J18, which are mapped to the general pneumonia diagnosis.
features.description: Indicates whether the patient has a diagnosis of pneumonia.
features.measurement_definition: Identify the presence of a pneumonia diagnosis, including mentions of 'pneumonia', 'community acquired pneumonia', or the ICD-10 code J18, within the patient record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Absent' if no mention of a pneumonia diagnosis is found in the clinical documentation.
features.name: pneumonia_diagnosis
features.stability_summary: The diagnosis is strongly supported by explicit mentions of pneumonia and the associated ICD-10 code J18 (pneumonia, unspecified organism).

features.caveats: Dependent on the administration of gadolinium-based contrast and the radiologist's interpretation of what constitutes 'abnormal' enhancement.
features.description: Presence of abnormal contrast enhancement in the posterior fossa.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether abnormal contrast enhancement is identified in the posterior fossa (including the cerebellar hemispheres and brainstem) from post-contrast T1-weighted imaging reports.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the posterior fossa is not mentioned, if contrast was not administered, or if the report is ambiguous regarding enhancement in this region.
features.name: posterior_fossa_enhancement
features.stability_summary: Abnormal enhancement in the posterior fossa is a standard finding reported during neuro-imaging (specifically post-contrast T1) to identify lesions, inflammation, or metastatic disease.

features.caveats: Reliance on radiologist's subjective interpretation of 'mass effect' without standardized quantitative metrics like midline shift or specific cistern measurements.
features.description: Presence of mass effect within the posterior fossa.
features.measurement_definition: Identify whether the imaging report indicates the presence or absence of mass effect in the posterior fossa (including the cerebellum and brainstem). Explicit statements such as 'no mass effect' map to 'Absent', while statements of mass effect or associated compressive findings map to 'Present'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the posterior fossa is not mentioned or if the presence/absence of mass effect is not documented.
features.name: posterior_fossa_mass_effect
features.stability_summary: Imaging reports typically provide a clear binary assessment of whether mass effect is present in the posterior fossa.

features.caveats: The ontology captures the binary occurrence of radiation therapy regardless of the site, modality (e.g., EBRT, SRS), or dosage.
features.description: Indication of whether the patient has a history of radiation therapy prior to the current clinical assessment.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient has received any form of radiation therapy (e.g., palliative thoracic radiation, whole-brain radiation, stereotactic radiosurgery/SRS, external beam radiation therapy/EBRT) from the patient's past medical history, oncology consultation notes, or review of systems.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the medical record is silent on radiation therapy or is ambiguous; represent as 'No' if previous radiation therapy is explicitly denied.
features.name: previous_radiation_therapy
features.stability_summary: Radiation history is a stable clinical attribute documented using standard terminology in oncology records.

features.caveats: Does not capture sub-lobar segmental locations or bilateral primary tumors.
features.description: The anatomical location of the primary lung tumor.
features.measurement_definition: The specific lobe of the lung where the primary tumor is located, extracted from radiology reports (e.g., CT, PET/CT) or surgical/biopsy pathology reports.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Unspecified' if the lobe is not documented or the location is ambiguous.
features.name: primary_tumor_location
features.stability_summary: The primary tumor location is a stable baseline characteristic determined by imaging and histopathology.

features.caveats: Morphological descriptions are qualitative and may vary based on the radiologist's interpretation and the imaging modality used.
features.description: The descriptive morphological characteristic of the primary tumor's shape or margins.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the descriptive term characterizing the primary tumor's morphology (e.g., 'spiculated', 'lobulated', 'irregular', 'smooth', 'circumscribed') from the radiology or pathology reports in the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no morphological description is provided in the record.
features.name: primary_tumor_morphology
features.stability_summary: Primary tumor morphology is typically derived from imaging and remains relatively stable over short intervals, though it may change in response to therapy.

features.caveats: Tumor size may be reported as a single dimension (e.g., 4.5 cm) or as three dimensions (e.g., 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.5 cm); in the latter case, the greatest dimension should be extracted.
features.description: The greatest dimension of the primary lung tumor.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the maximum diameter of the primary lung tumor from the pretreatment record, typically found in radiology reports (CT, PET/CT) or surgical pathology reports, measured in centimeters.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no numeric tumor size is documented or if the documentation is ambiguous.
features.name: primary_tumor_size
features.stability_summary: Tumor size is consistently documented as a numeric value in centimeters across imaging and pathology evidence.

features.caveats: Records may use the general term 'platinum-based chemotherapy' rather than specifying the exact agent (e.g., cisplatin, carboplatin).
features.description: Whether the patient has a history of receiving platinum-based chemotherapy prior to the current treatment context.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient has received chemotherapy containing a platinum agent (e.g., cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin) from the past medical history, oncology progress notes, or discharge summaries.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the record does not mention chemotherapy or the specific agents used.
features.name: prior_platinum_chemotherapy
features.stability_summary: The feature is well-supported by clinical documentation, which frequently explicitly lists 'platinum-based chemotherapy' or specific agents like 'cisplatin' in the context of NSCLC treatment.

features.caveats: The listed categories are derived from the provided evidence; a comprehensive list of all possible oncology regimens is too vast to enumerate fully in this ontology.
features.description: The name or description of the systemic therapy regimen administered to the patient prior to the current assessment.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the specific name of the chemotherapy or immunotherapy regimen(s) mentioned in the patient's history. This includes specific drug combinations (e.g., 'cisplatin/vinorelbine'), single agents (e.g., 'docetaxel'), or general clinical descriptions (e.g., 'platinum-free doublet').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Not documented' if no prior systemic treatment regimen is mentioned in the record.
features.name: prior_treatment_regimen
features.stability_summary: Prior treatment regimens are typically explicitly documented in oncology records as part of the patient's cancer history, though they may be described with varying levels of specificity ranging from specific drug pairs to general class descriptions.

features.caveats: The evidence specifies a 0-4 scale; while CTCAE generally goes to 5, PRO-CTCAE is typically constrained to 0-4 for severity.
features.description: Patient-reported severity of pain according to the PRO-CTCAE instrument.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical grade (0, 1, 2, 3, or 4) for pain severity from the PRO-CTCAE instrument section of the patient record. If reported as 'X/4', extract 'X'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the PRO-CTCAE pain severity is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: pro_ctcae_pain_severity
features.stability_summary: The feature is based on the standardized PRO-CTCAE instrument, which consistently uses an ordinal 0-4 scale to quantify patient-reported symptom severity.

features.caveats: The term 'progressive' is subjective and relies on clinician interpretation of patient history or longitudinal documentation.
features.description: Presence of symptoms triggered by physical exertion that have worsened in frequency or severity over time.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient record indicates symptoms (e.g., dyspnea, angina, or fatigue) that occur during exertion and are described as progressive or worsening.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if documentation of exertional symptoms or their progression is absent or ambiguous.
features.name: progressive_exertional_symptoms
features.stability_summary: Documentation of progressive exertional symptoms is a standard clinical indicator of declining functional capacity in cardiovascular and pulmonary contexts.

features.caveats: PPI use may be documented as a specific medication name (e.g., omeprazole) rather than the class name.
features.description: Patient use of proton pump inhibitor (PPI) medication prior to treatment.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is documented as taking a proton pump inhibitor (e.g., omeprazole, pantoprazole, lansoprazole, esomeprazole, rabeprazole) from the medication list or clinical history.
features.missing_value_rule: If PPI use is not documented or the documentation is ambiguous, represent as null.
features.name: proton_pump_inhibitor_use
features.stability_summary: PPI use is a standard clinical data point typically found in medication histories or records regarding gastroesophageal reflux disease.

features.caveats: The supporting evidence provided is highly fragmented and lacks sufficient clinical detail to specify particular psychiatric symptoms or diagnostic criteria.
features.description: A binary indicator of whether psychiatric symptoms are documented in the patient's pretreatment record.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the presence or absence of any documented psychiatric symptoms or diagnoses from the pretreatment medical records.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if there is no documentation or the documentation is ambiguous regarding the presence of psychiatric symptoms.
features.name: psychiatric_symptom_presence
features.stability_summary: The ontology is derived primarily from the feature name as a binary presence indicator, as the provided evidence text is insufficiently descriptive.

features.caveats: The supporting evidence is highly fragmented and does not specify a particular diagnosis, only a general reference to 'bilateral pulmonary'.
features.description: Presence of a documented pulmonary condition.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient record contains a diagnosis or a clinical finding indicating a pulmonary condition (e.g., COPD, asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, or other bilateral pulmonary pathologies).
features.missing_value_rule: If no pulmonary condition is documented or the information is ambiguous, it is represented as 'Absent'.
features.name: pulmonary_condition
features.stability_summary: The phrase 'bilateral pulmonary' suggests a pulmonary process, supporting the extraction of a binary pulmonary condition indicator.

features.caveats: Does not capture the quantity, size, or stability of nodules.
features.description: Presence of pulmonary nodules in the lungs.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether pulmonary nodules are reported in the pretreatment imaging (typically CT chest). A report of 'no pulmonary nodules' or 'no new pulmonary nodules' indicates 'absent'. The mention of any pulmonary nodule, regardless of size or novelty, indicates 'present'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no imaging reports are available or if pulmonary nodules are not mentioned.
features.name: pulmonary_nodules_presence
features.stability_summary: Standard radiologic finding reported in routine thoracic imaging surveillance.

features.caveats: Clinical documentation often couples reactivity with symmetry (e.g., 'equal and reactive'); only the reactivity component should be extracted for this feature.
features.description: The response of the pupils to light stimulation
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the pupils are documented as reactive or non-reactive to light from the neurological or physical examination section of the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if pupil reactivity is not documented or is described ambiguously.
features.name: pupil_reactivity
features.stability_summary: Pupil reactivity is a standard component of the neurological physical exam and is typically recorded as a binary state.

features.caveats: Scores are typically mapped to a 0-100 scale; the raw numeric score should be extracted.
features.description: Patient-reported score of physical function from the EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value for Physical Function (often denoted as Physical or Physical Function) from the EORTC QLQ-C30 instrument.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the Physical Function score is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: qlq_c30_physical_function
features.stability_summary: The EORTC QLQ-C30 Physical Function scale is a validated patient-reported outcome measure assessing a patient's ability to perform physical activities.

features.caveats: Values are transformed scores; raw item responses are not captured.
features.description: Patient-reported role functioning score from the EORTC QLQ-C30 quality of life instrument.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value for 'Role Function' (or 'Role') from the EORTC QLQ-C30 assessment. If the score is reported as a fraction (e.g., '70/100'), extract the numerator.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the EORTC QLQ-C30 Role Function score is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: qlq_c30_role_function
features.stability_summary: Standardized patient-reported outcome measure for role functioning using the EORTC QLQ-C30 instrument, typically reported on a 0-100 scale.

features.caveats: The evidence does not specify the anatomical site or target of the radiosurgery, which may be clinically relevant.
features.description: History of radiosurgery or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) prior to the pretreatment record.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient record contains any mention of prior radiosurgery or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), including terms such as 'post-srs' or specific SRS dosing (e.g., 'srs 12 gy').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if there is no mention of radiosurgery; represent as null if the documentation specifically suggests the history is unknown or ambiguous.
features.name: radiosurgery_history
features.stability_summary: The feature is supported by multiple explicit mentions of radiosurgery and the common abbreviation SRS, including a specific radiation dose, confirming its presence in the clinical records.

features.caveats: Qualitative descriptors of breathing patterns (e.g., 'tachypneic', 'normal') without a numeric count are excluded from extraction.
features.description: The number of breaths taken by the patient per minute.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value for respiratory rate (RR) from the vital signs section of the pretreatment clinical record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the respiratory rate is not documented or is provided only as a non-numeric description.
features.name: respiratory_rate
features.stability_summary: Respiratory rate is a standard clinical vital sign used to evaluate pulmonary and cardiovascular stability.

features.caveats: The extraction relies on the radiologist's explicit qualitative assessment; a finding of 'acute infarction' without the specific phrase 'restricted diffusion' should be interpreted based on clinical context but mapped here only if DWI/ADC is the supporting evidence.
features.description: Presence of restricted diffusion on Diffusion Weighted Imaging (DWI) and Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC) maps.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the presence or absence of restricted diffusion from the radiology report's DWI/ADC findings section. 'No areas of restricted diffusion' maps to 'Absent'; mentions of restricted diffusion as a finding map to 'Present'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if DWI/ADC imaging was not performed or if restricted diffusion is not mentioned.
features.name: restricted_diffusion_on_dwi_adc
features.stability_summary: Restricted diffusion on DWI/ADC is a standard clinical radiologic marker used to identify acute ischemic stroke or highly cellular lesions.

features.caveats: Documentation may specify 'new' nodes or provide specific measurements; any finding consistent with lymphadenopathy in the retroperitoneal space should be classified as Present.
features.description: Presence of enlarged lymph nodes in the retroperitoneal region.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the pretreatment clinical records or imaging reports indicate the presence of retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
features.missing_value_rule: If the records do not mention retroperitoneal lymph nodes or their status, represent as null.
features.name: retroperitoneal_lymphadenopathy_presence
features.stability_summary: Retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy is a standard radiological finding used in oncological staging and treatment eligibility assessments.

features.caveats: Evidence is based on a small set of phrases; extraction depends on the explicit mention of scapular involvement.
features.description: Presence of metastatic disease in the scapula.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if the pretreatment record indicates the presence of metastasis in the scapula (e.g., 'known scapular metastasis', 'scapular metastasis').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the documentation is absent or does not specify the presence or absence of scapular metastasis.
features.name: scapular_metastasis
features.stability_summary: The clinical evidence explicitly lists 'scapular metastasis' and 'known scapular metastasis', supporting a binary ontology for the presence of this condition.

features.caveats: Albumin levels can be influenced by the patient's hydration status, acute phase response to inflammation, and liver or kidney function.
features.description: The concentration of albumin in the patient's serum.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value for serum albumin from the pretreatment laboratory records, typically reported as part of a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP).
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the value is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: serum_albumin
features.stability_summary: Serum albumin is a standard biochemical measurement used to evaluate nutritional status and systemic inflammation, typically reported in grams per deciliter.

features.caveats: In most clinical laboratory reports (such as the CMP), the CO2 value represents total carbon dioxide, which is primarily composed of serum bicarbonate.
features.description: The concentration of bicarbonate in the patient's serum, typically measured as part of a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP).
features.measurement_definition: Extract the serum bicarbonate level, typically listed as CO2 or HCO3 in the laboratory data section of the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the value is not documented or is ambiguous.
features.name: serum_bicarbonate
features.stability_summary: Serum bicarbonate is a standard clinical measurement used to evaluate the acid-base balance of the blood.

features.caveats: Values may be reported as total or corrected (albumin-adjusted) calcium; extraction should prioritize the reported value.
features.description: The concentration of calcium in the patient's serum.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the most recent numeric value for serum calcium measured in mg/dL from the pretreatment clinical record.
features.missing_value_rule: If serum calcium is not documented or is ambiguous, return null.
features.name: serum_calcium
features.stability_summary: Serum calcium is a standard laboratory marker used to assess calcium homeostasis and identify hypercalcemia or hypocalcemia.

features.caveats: None
features.description: The concentration of chloride ions in the patient's serum.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value for serum chloride (often abbreviated as 'Cl') from the pretreatment laboratory records, typically found within a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP).
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the serum chloride measurement is missing or ambiguous.
features.name: serum_chloride
features.stability_summary: Serum chloride is a standard electrolyte measurement typically reported in mmol/L as part of a basic or comprehensive metabolic panel.

features.caveats: Units may be reported as mmol/L, which are equivalent to mEq/L for sodium.
features.description: The concentration of sodium ions in the patient's blood serum.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value for serum sodium (commonly abbreviated as 'Na') from the Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP) or a basic electrolyte panel in the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if serum sodium is not documented or the value is ambiguous.
features.name: serum_sodium
features.stability_summary: Serum sodium is a standard clinical laboratory measurement typically reported as part of a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP) using consistent units of mEq/L or mmol/L.

features.caveats: None
features.description: Biological sex of the patient.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the patient's biological sex from the pretreatment medical record, typically found in the patient demographics, header, or pathology report patient information section.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if not documented or ambiguous.
features.name: sex
features.stability_summary: Biological sex is a stable patient-level demographic characteristic consistently documented across clinical and pathology records.

features.caveats: Extraction is limited to explicit mention of the skull base and calvarium in the context of lytic or sclerotic bone changes.
features.description: Presence of lytic or sclerotic lesions at the skull base.
features.measurement_definition: Identify whether the imaging report explicitly states the presence or absence of lytic or sclerotic lesions in the skull base or calvarium.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the skull base is not mentioned or if there is no statement regarding lytic or sclerotic lesions.
features.name: skull_base_lytic_sclerotic_lesions
features.stability_summary: Lytic and sclerotic lesions are standard radiological findings used to identify bone metastases or other skeletal pathologies in the cranial region.

features.caveats: Duration is typically reported in years; other time units (e.g., months) may require normalization to years for consistency.
features.description: The length of time since the patient stopped smoking.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the duration since the patient ceased smoking, categorized as <= 5 years, 5-10 years, or > 10 years, as documented in the pretreatment records.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if smoking cessation duration is not documented or the patient is a current smoker.
features.name: smoking_cessation_duration
features.stability_summary: Clinical evidence shows reported durations of smoking cessation explicitly stated in years (e.g., 'quit 5 years', 'quit 10 years').

features.caveats: Pack-year history is a separate quantitative measure and should not be incorporated into the categorical smoking status.
features.description: The patient's lifetime tobacco use status.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the patient's smoking status from the social history, past medical history, or review of systems. Identify whether the patient has never used tobacco, used tobacco in the past but has since quit, or is currently using tobacco.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'Unknown' if the documentation is absent, ambiguous, or contradictory without a clear timeline.
features.name: smoking_status
features.stability_summary: Smoking status is a standard clinical data point documented across various sections of medical records, typically appearing as a distinct category in social history.

features.caveats: Different assay sensitivities (e.g., Variant Allele Frequency thresholds) may result in discordant findings between different genomic tests.
features.description: The mutation status of the STK11 gene, specifically whether a pathogenic alteration or loss of function is present.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the STK11 genomic status from molecular pathology or next-generation sequencing (NGS) reports. Any report of a pathogenic mutation, 'loss', 'loss-of-function', or 'homozygous deletion' is mapped to 'Mutated'. Reports of 'wild-type' or 'no pathogenic variants detected' are mapped to 'Wild-type'.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if STK11 status is not documented or explicitly listed as unknown.
features.name: stk11_mutation_status
features.stability_summary: Determined via DNA sequencing; mutation status is generally consistent across tumor biopsies, although subclonal heterogeneity can occur.

features.caveats: Detection depends on the sensitivity of the imaging modality used (e.g., CT or MRI) and the timing of the scan relative to the hemorrhagic event.
features.description: Presence of subdural hemorrhage
features.measurement_definition: Extract the presence or absence of subdural hemorrhage from pretreatment imaging reports or clinical documentation. Mark as 'present' if a subdural hemorrhage or subdural hematoma is identified; mark as 'absent' if the report explicitly states no subdural hemorrhage is present.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the records do not mention the presence or absence of subdural hemorrhage.
features.name: subdural_hemorrhage
features.stability_summary: Subdural hemorrhage is a standard clinical finding identified via neuroimaging, typically characterized by a collection of blood between the dura mater and the arachnoid layer.

features.caveats: The ontology simplifies the descriptive appearance into a binary state and does not distinguish between opposing pathological states such as effacement (suggesting edema) and prominence (suggesting atrophy).
features.description: Qualitative assessment of the cerebral sulci and cisterns on neuroimaging.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the description of the cerebral sulci and cisterns from the imaging report. Assign 'unremarkable' for descriptors indicating a normal appearance (e.g., 'unremarkable', 'normal', 'within normal limits') and 'abnormal' for any description of pathology (e.g., 'effaced', 'widened', 'prominent', 'narrowed').
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the documentation is absent or does not explicitly describe the appearance of the sulci and cisterns.
features.name: sulci_and_cisterns_appearance
features.stability_summary: Based on standard neuroimaging reporting where 'unremarkable' indicates the absence of structural abnormalities such as cortical atrophy or cerebral edema.

features.caveats: Systolic blood pressure is typically recorded as part of a systolic/diastolic pair; the systolic value is the first number listed.
features.description: The pressure in the patient's arteries during the contraction of the heart ventricle.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the first numeric value (the systolic component) from the blood pressure reading (e.g., from '128/74 mmHg', extract '128') found in the physical examination or vital signs section of the pretreatment record.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if systolic blood pressure is not documented or if the documentation is too ambiguous to extract a numeric value.
features.name: systolic_blood_pressure
features.stability_summary: Blood pressure is a standard, universally measured clinical vital sign with high stability and reproducibility across clinical settings.

features.caveats: T-stage definitions may vary slightly between AJCC editions; extraction assumes the most recent reported staging version.
features.description: The T (primary tumor) component of the TNM staging system for lung cancer, describing the size and extent of the primary tumor.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the T-stage value from the TNM classification string (e.g., 'T3' from 'T3N2M1' or 'pT2a' from 'pT2aN2'). Remove prefixes such as 'p' (pathological) or 'c' (clinical) to isolate the scalar T-category.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the T-stage is not explicitly documented or is listed as TX.
features.name: t_stage
features.stability_summary: T-stage is a standardized, internationally recognized metric within the TNM staging system used to describe the primary tumor's anatomical extent in oncology.

features.caveats: Generic mentions of 'inhaler' or 'puffs' without the specific drug name tiotropium are insufficient to establish use.
features.description: Indicates whether the patient was using tiotropium prior to the start of treatment.
features.measurement_definition: Identify if tiotropium is listed in the patient's medication records, prescriptions, or mentioned as a current medication in clinical notes.
features.missing_value_rule: If no documentation of tiotropium use is present or if the documentation is ambiguous, represent as 'No'.
features.name: tiotropium_use
features.stability_summary: Tiotropium is a well-defined pharmaceutical agent used in the management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; its use can be reliably identified via explicit mention in medical records.

features.caveats: The feature represents a general finding of tissue thickening without specifying the anatomical location.
features.description: Presence of abnormal tissue thickening.
features.measurement_definition: Extract whether the clinical record indicates the presence of tissue thickening.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the documentation does not mention tissue thickening or is ambiguous.
features.name: tissue_thickening
features.stability_summary: Tissue thickening is a common qualitative clinical finding reported in imaging and pathology.

features.caveats: Extraction depends on the availability of the specific pack-year calculation; patients described only as 'smoker' or 'former smoker' without a quantity cannot be assigned a continuous value.
features.description: Total cumulative tobacco smoking exposure measured in pack-years.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the total number of pack-years of smoking history from the patient's social or medical history. If the patient is explicitly documented as a 'never smoker', the value is 0.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if smoking status is not mentioned, or if the patient is identified as a current or former smoker but no numeric pack-year value is provided.
features.name: tobacco_smoking_history

features.description: Detection status of the TP53 R273H mutation in tumor tissue.

features.name: tp53_r273h_mutation_status
features.stability_summary: TP53 R273H is a common somatic hotspot mutation in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) associated with genomic instability and poor prognosis.

features.caveats: Extraction often relies on patient-reported subjective approximations rather than clinical scale measurements.
features.description: The total amount of unintentional weight loss experienced by the patient prior to the start of treatment.
features.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of unintentional weight loss reported in the pretreatment record. If the value is provided in pounds (lb), convert to kilograms (kg) by dividing by 2.20462. If only a qualitative statement of weight loss (e.g., 'positive for weight loss') is provided without a specific quantity, it cannot be mapped to this continuous scalar.
features.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if weight change is not documented, is explicitly denied, or is mentioned qualitatively without a numeric value.
features.name: unintended_weight_change
features.stability_summary: Weight loss is frequently reported as a quantified constitutional symptom in the provided evidence, typically measured in kilograms or pounds.

features.caveats: Variant allele frequency can exhibit significant spatial heterogeneity across different biopsy sites within the same patient.
features.description: The proportion of sequencing reads carrying a specific genetic variant relative to the total number of reads at that genomic position.

features.missing_value_rule: If the variant allele frequency is not explicitly reported or is ambiguous, the value is null.
features.name: variant_allele_frequency
features.stability_summary: VAF is a standard quantitative metric in next-generation sequencing (NGS) used to estimate the prevalence of a mutation in a sample.

features.stability_summary: The feature is explicitly documented in radiology reports using standardized terminology (e.g., 'surrounding vasogenic edema', 'no adjacent edema'), providing a high degree of reproducibility.

features.name: ventricular_size
features.stability_summary: Ventricular size is a standard neuroimaging observation used to identify potential hydrocephalus or cerebral atrophy.
